chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from al-Sayyārī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said to me: “The Shiʿah have been nurtured by hopes for two hundred years.”

He said: Yaqṭīn said to his son ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, “Why is it that what was said to us happened, while what was said to you did not happen?” He said: So ʿAlī said to him, “What was said to us and to you came from one source, except that your matter became present, so you were given its pure reality, and it occurred just as was said to you. But our matter has not yet arrived, so we were consoled with hopes. If it had been said to us that this matter would not happen until two hundred years or three hundred years, hearts would have hardened and most people would have turned back from Islam. But they said, ‘How swift it is, and how near it is,’ to draw together the hearts of the people and to bring the relief near.”
Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim ibn Ismāʿīl al-Anbārī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mihzam, from his father, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

We mentioned in his presence the kings of the family of so-and-so, so he said: “People only perished because of their hastening regarding this matter. Indeed, Allah does not hasten because of the haste of the servants. Surely, for this matter there is an end-point to which it comes; when they reach it, they will neither advance it by an hour nor delay it.”

key_terms.اسْتِعْجَالِهِمْ: their seeking to hasten the matter before its appointed time
key_terms.الشِّيعَةُ: the Shiʿah, the followers devoted to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْأَمَانِيِّ: hopes or expectations by which people were sustained
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which people might have turned back under severe delay
key_terms.الْعِبَادِ: the servants, meaning human beings before Allah
key_terms.الْفَرَجِ: relief, the awaited easing and resolution
key_terms.غَايَةً: a fixed endpoint or appointed limit
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: this matter, the divinely appointed affair being discussed

ai.seo_question: Why do narrations say the Shiʿah were sustained by hope regarding the divine affair, and can its time be hastened?
ai.summary: This report speaks about the prolonged expectation surrounding the divinely appointed matter and explains that believers were sustained through hope so that their hearts would remain firm. It also teaches that the divine affair has a fixed term set by Allah, and human haste cannot bring it forward or delay it.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and Ahmad Bin Idrees from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Sayyari, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from his brother Al Husayn, from his father Ali Bin Yaqteen who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said to me: ‘The Shias have been nourished with the belief since two hundred years’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And Yaqteen said to his son Ali Bin Yaqteen, ‘What is the matter that what was said to us, happened, and (what) was said to you all, so it did not happen?’ So Ali said to him, ‘That which was said to us and to you was from one exit, apart from that your matter was present, so it was given to you purely. So if happened just as it had been said to you. And our matter is not present (i.e., it is for the future), so we have aspirations, and if it had been said to us that this matter would not be happening except after two hundred years or three hundred years, the hearts would have hardened and the generality of the people would return from Al-Islam. But, theyasws were saying: ‘How fast it would be and how close’, in order to harmonise the hearts of the people and the imminence of the relief.[942]  (This is not a Hadith) Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Ismail Al Anbary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘We mentioned the kinship of the family of so and so in hisasws presence, so heasws said: ‘But rather, the people perished due to their haste for this matter. Allahazwj does not Make Haste due to the haste of the servants. For this matter there is a goal it would be ending up to. So if it has reached it, it would neither be brought forward by a moment nor would it be delayed’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Idris have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following.
“Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) said to me, ‘The Shi‘a have live on hopes for two hundred years.’”

The narrator has said that Yaqtin said to his son, Ali ibn Yaqtin, “We did not have to worry. What was said to us came true. What is said to you has not come true yet” Ali then said to him, “What was said to you and what is said to us all come from one source except that good news for you have come true and you received it pure. It was just as was said to be. The good news for us has not yet come true. We thus, entertain ourselves with hopes. If we would be told that it will take place after two or three hundred years our hearts will harden and the masses will turn back from Islam. However, they have said that it will come very soon and in near future to encourage people about the coming of the relief.”
